content.text: No JVM metrics exist for auth-service. I'll run a broad sweep across all services and metrics (gauges and sums), flagging the largest mean shifts to find anything the survey missed.

input.query: WITH n AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric m, avg(value) nv, stddev(value) ns FROM normal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2), a AS (SELECT service_name svc, metric m, avg(value) av FROM abnormal_metrics GROUP BY 1,2) SELECT n.svc, n.m, round(n.nv,3) nv, round(a.av,3) av, round((a.av-n.nv)/nullif(n.ns,0),2) z FROM n JOIN a USING (svc,m) WHERE abs(a.av-n.nv) > 0.2*abs(n.nv) AND abs(a.av-n.nv)>1e-6 AND n.m NOT LIKE 'k8s.pod.uptime' ORDER BY abs(z) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 40

content.text: Two things stand out: the admin-user pod filesystem usage jumped (27 MB → 37 MB), and the admin POST client span (~720 ms p95) is much longer than the auth server span (~288 ms p95). That gap could be time on the wire. I'll join the two spans per trace to measure it directly.

input.query: SELECT c.trace_id, c.duration/1e6 client_ms, s.duration/1e6 server_ms, (c.duration - s.duration)/1e6 gap_ms, s.attr_k8s_pod_name auth_pod, c.attr_k8s_pod_name admin_pod, s.span_name FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON c.trace_id=s.trace_id AND s.parent_span_id=c.span_id WHERE c.service_name='ts-admin-user-service' AND c.span_name='POST' AND c.attr_span_kind='Client' ORDER BY c.duration DESC LIMIT 40
